record.paper_title: Highlights and Open Questions from ZEUS
record.context_brief: Mechanism behind W dependence of diffraction
record.original_question: The ratio of the diffractive contribution to the total virtual-photon-proton cross-section is approximately constant as a function of W for several MX intervals, even though the naive expectation would be that the diffractive contribution rises twice as quickly as the total cross-section because it is associated with the forward part of the scattering amplitude. What dynamical mechanism is responsible for the observed W dependence of the diffractive cross-section?

evidence.quote: An approximately constant ratio with W indicates a diffractive contribution which rises with a similar W dependence. This simple observation is contrary to the naïve expectation where the diffractive contribution is identified with the forward part of the scattering amplitude and would therefore rise twice as quickly as the total cross-section as a function of W.
In order to understand the driving mechanism responsible for this rise, the cross-sections at fixed MX and W are plotted in terms of scaling variables.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider deep inelastic scattering of a virtual photon (γ*) of virtuality Q² on a proton at center-of-mass energy W. Let σ_tot(γ*p)(W,Q²) denote the total virtual-photon–proton cross section, and let dσ^diff/dM_X (W, Q², M_X) denote the differential diffractive cross section at fixed invariant mass M_X of the diffractively produced hadronic system. The optical theorem and the identification of diffraction with the forward (elastic) part of the scattering amplitude would naively imply that σ_diff scales like (σ_tot)², so that the ratio σ_diff/σ_tot grows like a power of W. Empirically, however, for several intervals of M_X, the ratio of the diffractive contribution to the total virtual-photon-proton cross section is found to be approximately independent of W, meaning that σ_diff and σ_tot have nearly the same W dependence.

Problem: Identify and characterize the dynamical mechanism responsible for the observed W dependence of the diffractive cross section in deep inelastic γ*p scattering. Specifically, determine why dσ^diff/dM_X rises with W at the same rate as σ_tot(γ*p) rather than twice as fast as predicted by the naive forward-amplitude argument, and express this mechanism in terms of suitable scaling variables (e.g., the Bjorken-like variable β = Q²/(Q² + M_X²) and x_IP = (Q² + M_X²)/(Q² + W²)) and/or an effective exchanged trajectory.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent ZEUS and H1 analyses interpret the observed W dependence in terms of pomeron exchange with an effective trajectory α_IP(0) ≈ 1.12–1.13, somewhat larger than the soft-pomeron intercept seen in hadronic total cross sections. The data are consistent with Regge factorization of the diffractive structure function and with QCD-based dipole / two-gluon exchange descriptions that incorporate (controlled) factorization breaking. Thus the qualitative mechanism (pomeron / two-gluon exchange in a dipole picture) is established and matches measurements, but a fully first-principles QCD derivation of the diffractive W dependence is still being refined.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the Diffractive Cross Section in Deep Inelastic Scattering using ZEUS 1994 Data
status_evidence.snippet: a^diff = 0.507 ± 0.034 ... t-averaged pomeron trajectory ≈ 1.127; the W dependence of the diffractive cross section is the same as that of the total γ*p cross section.
status_evidence.claim: The diffractive cross section rises with W with an effective pomeron trajectory ~1.13, matching σ_tot(γ*p), explained via pomeron exchange.

status_evidence.title: Diffraction at HERA: experimental perspective
status_evidence.snippet: Diffractive DIS at HERA is described in terms of pomeron exchange / two-gluon exchange in a dipole picture consistent with factorization.
status_evidence.claim: The dynamical mechanism is identified with pomeron / two-gluon exchange, and data are consistent with diffractive factorization.
